clue.text: When a dull queen met old king at court in reality

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
matt describes a dull, unshiny finish
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen
Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia

explanation.surface: A tale of a drab queen meeting an ancient king at court, told as though it really happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'met' is only a link joining the pieces. Offa, the old king, is the Anglo-Saxon ruler famous for Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms meaning actually or in truth, introducing a statement of fact.

clue.text: Cut superfluous joke

parts.note: spare means surplus to needs, superfluous
to rib someone is to joke with or tease them

explanation.surface: An instruction to delete an unnecessary gag from a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb telling you to remove the joke, but it is a noun: a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a butcher's cut of pork from the ribs, an example of a cut of meat.

clue.text: Academic suppresses old evidence

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down or keep in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic

explanation.surface: A scholar hiding outdated findings, a small research scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that establishes a fact, so the two are synonyms in this sense.

clue.text: How Ibsen transformed part in The Wild Duck?

indicators.note: something transformed has been changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about how Ibsen reworked a role in his play The Wild Duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wild Duck is a play by Ibsen, so 'part' looks like a stage role; read literally, it is a body part of a wild duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The wishbone is the forked bone in a bird's breast, so it is literally a part found in any duck.

clue.text: We might shed mass losing it

definitions.text: We might shed mass losing it

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so a letter is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A dieter's remark: losing it is how we would shed some mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Take WE and MIGHT, then shed the M for mass. The whole clue also describes the answer: 'it' is what we lose when we shed mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing weight means shedding body mass, so the thing lost is exactly what the clue calls 'it'.

clue.text: Champion ducks taking part in pitch for coach's job

indicators.note: taking part in means entering into, so these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: to sling is to throw or pitch
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, and two noughts look like OO

explanation.surface: A champion bowler ducking out of a pitch, which sounds like work for the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so two ducks give two O's.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach trains and instructs pupils, and schooling is that training or instruction.

clue.text: Soldier receives second posh volume

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the soldier holds the other pieces

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker ant, so soldier gives ANT
a mo is a moment or second
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A soldier getting a second, rather grand book.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U is an old British label for upper-class versus ordinary speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume and amount are both words for a quantity of something.

clue.text: To have impact, give notice if about to open barrier

parts.note: to make an ad is to give public notice

indicators.note: to open something here is to split it apart by going into it

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Advice on announcing a plan before breaking through a barrier, to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe having an effect, so they are equivalent idioms.

clue.text: Manage drink before about a quarter past six

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: past means after, so this piece follows

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
S, south, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone planning to have a drink at about a quarter past six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter past six' reads as a time, but it is S placed after VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage people or a task is to oversee or direct it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Mark and Charlie knock back rounds

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: knock back suggests sending something back the way it came, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rounds of ammunition are ammo

explanation.surface: Two drinkers called Mark and Charlie downing rounds at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a drinking companion's name, but it is the definition: a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is a punctuation mark, so it is an example of a mark.

clue.text: Media boss often defends Republican party

indicators.note: to defend is to guard by surrounding, so one piece shields the other

parts.note: much can mean often, as in 'do you go there much?'
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A media mogul regularly standing up for the Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Murdoch is a famous newspaper and television proprietor, an example of a media boss.

clue.text: Drop version of EU blog about Luxembourg

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the letter
a version of something is a reworked form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A European Union blog post about Luxembourg being dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A globule is a small round drop of liquid, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Group of operators withdrawing carriage allowance

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the letters are read backwards
a group of the letters of operators is taken out of the word

explanation.surface: A group of firms pulling out of a transport subsidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tare is the weight allowed for a vehicle or container, deducted to find the weight of the goods carried.

clue.text: Claimed petty officer delayed visiting boss

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a stud is a raised boss or knob
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A petty officer claiming they were held up while visiting the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager, but it is a stud, a raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: To postulate is to put forward as true or claim, so the past forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Do this while waiting to go up for cosmetic procedures?

definitions.text: Do this while waiting to go up for cosmetic procedures?

parts.words: Do this while waiting to go up for cosmetic procedures?
parts.note: someone waiting for an elevator stands looking at the doors, so they are literally facing the lifts

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about what to do while waiting to ascend.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer describes standing turned towards the lifts; read as one, it names surgery that tightens the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic operations tighten facial skin, and the phrase also describes standing turned towards elevators.

clue.text: Hug English married couple

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple

explanation.surface: An English newly-wed pair sharing a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to hold them in your arms, a synonym for hugging.

clue.text: See chief quietly concerning dispute

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly
on means about or concerning
a tiff is a minor dispute

explanation.surface: An instruction to quietly visit the boss about a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: the Holy See, the Pope's jurisdiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope heads the Holy See, so he is the chief of that See.

clue.text: Varied portions matter but not much

indicators.note: varied means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that differing portion sizes are of little consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter but not much' sounds like 'it hardly matters', but it describes a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A positron is an antimatter particle, the electron's positive counterpart, a minute speck of matter.

clue.text: Tenants terribly upset about heroin addict at first

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the phrase goes round the letters

parts.note: in bits is an informal phrase for very distressed

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Residents greatly distressed about a heroin addict in the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenants' looks like a plural noun, but here it is a verb: to tenant a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenant a property is to occupy it, the same sense as to dwell in or occupy.

clue.text: Free boating here in Sussex around harbour

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the phrase goes round the letter

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Sussex, so boating there is on the Ouse
H is the abbreviation for harbour on maps

explanation.surface: An offer of free boating in a Sussex harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink on the house is provided free by the establishment, an idiom for free of charge.

clue.text: Arm band and revolutionary force

definitions.meaning: a twisted metal ring or collar worn as an ornament, as by ancient Celts
in physics, the turning force that causes rotation

explanation.surface: An armband worn by a force of revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a twisted metal ornamental band and the rotational force in mechanics.

clue.text: Ring relatives lacking large units of 5

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: uncles are relatives

explanation.surface: A ring of relatives short of any large units.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' refers to the answer of 5 down, whose units these are.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounces are units in the imperial system for measuring how heavy something is, the subject of 5 down.

clue.text: Perhaps trainer has head office in Kent?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, so it gives SE

explanation.surface: A sports coach with headquarters in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England. 'trainer' suggests a coach, but it is a sports shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, so it is an example of footwear in the singular.

clue.text: The obvious point in conversation primarily

definitions.text: The obvious point in conversation primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A description of what a conversation is chiefly about.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion is the main thing talked about, the central point of a conversation.

clue.text: It's strange following old rule

parts.note: reign means rule

explanation.surface: A comment that it is odd still to follow an outdated rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean alien or unfamiliar, so it is a synonym of strange.

clue.text: He leaves the Russian unit upset

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian unit of currency

explanation.surface: A man walking out of a disturbed Russian army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unit' suggests a military unit, but it is a unit of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to disturb or distress them, a synonym of the verb upset.

clue.text: Business unit ignores international matter

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A business unit disregarding an international issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' looks like a noun, but here it is a verb: to be important.
explanation.definitionFit: To count is to be important or significant, as in 'every vote counts', so it is a synonym of matter.

clue.text: He earned his credit, some might say, in vain

indicators.note: this signals that the words are pronounced as some speakers would, dropping their aitches

parts.note: earned means got, and credit is tick, so in a dropped-aitch accent this is ''e got 'is tick'

explanation.surface: Someone who boasts that he earned his credit honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tick is British slang for credit. Dropping the h's, as in Cockney speech, gives ''e got 'is tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain person is self-centred and conceited, which is what this adjective describes.
